title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page, p. 120 of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie', Grothendieck), sitting among the 1976 handwritten notes on divided-power de Rham complexes. Most likely it is a recycled sheet whose blank side carries notes; it is stamped 438. Its content has nothing to do with the neighbouring pages, which build a simplicial object of divided-power dg-algebras from a coalgebra.

The mathematics, in modern language. K is the fraction field of a henselian discrete valuation ring V, and A_K is an abelian variety over K. A_K has potentially semistable reduction: it acquires semistable reduction over a finite extension K' with ring V' (S' = Spec V'). Exposé IX 9.1.2 defines the monodromy pairing for the semistable model over S'. This is a pairing between the character groups of the toric parts of the special fibres of the Néron models of A and of its dual A'. Restricted to the descended lattices M_K and M'_K, it gives v_ℓ^{K'} : M_K ⊗ M'_K → Z_ℓ(K).

Grothendieck normalizes it as u_ℓ = (1/e(S'/S)) v_ℓ^{K'}, where e = length(V'/m V') is the ramification index. This normalized pairing is independent of K', by 10.4.3. It is called the monodromy pairing of A_K. When A_K itself is semistable it agrees with the earlier pairing 9.1.2.

By 10.4 (the comparison with the pairing defined via Néron models and the Néron–Tate / Mumford-type biextension), u_ℓ takes values in Q(K) and does not depend on ℓ. Grothendieck then asks whether it is in fact Z-valued. He answers yes for elliptic curves: the only nontrivial case is potentially multiplicative reduction, where M ≅ M' has rank 1. Using Néron's results [19], the pairing equals the rational number v(j), the normalized valuation of the j-invariant (in absolute value it is the order of the Tate parameter q).
errors: Possible sign convention issue. For potentially multiplicative reduction v(j) < 0 and v(q) = -v(j) > 0. Exposé IX proves the monodromy pairing is (positive or negative) definite, so 'égal à v(j)' fixes a sign convention that one should check against 9.1.2 (some accounts would write -v(j)). Otherwise the page is correct; it is published text.

ideas.what: Monodromy pairing for abelian varieties with potentially semistable reduction, normalized by the ramification index e(S'/S) so that it is independent of the extension K'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA 7 I Exp. IX (1967-69, publ. 1972)

ideas.what: Rationality and ℓ-independence of the monodromy pairing via comparison with Néron-model data
Question of integrality of the normalized pairing; for elliptic curves it equals v(j), the valuation of the Tate parameter, computed via Néron
ideas.modern_name: Integrality of the monodromy pairing; Tate curve q-parameter

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed page of the published SGA 7 I Exposé IX (p. 120), apparently a recycled sheet in the archive folder. Everything on it is in print and credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The page is typescript from SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, p. 120 (archive stamp 438, pencil folio 123), not part of the handwritten de Rham notes.
Coefficient rings are typeset as Z_{ℓK}, Q_{ℓK}, Q_K, Z_K, i.e. the constant sheaves Z_ℓ, Q_ℓ, Q, Z on K (étale); the machine transcription renders them adequately.
